CRM data on 2440 dispute tickets shows a median response time of 1.6 days and p90 of 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA. Ticket handling is currently performing within SLA, so slow/backlogged response capacity does not appear to be the operative constraint right now.

The authoritative, complete billing-db tariff change log shows zero tariff change records, meaning no tariff schedule change occurred that could explain the disputed-bill errors via tariff misapplication tied to a rate update.

CRM dispute volume by month shows a stable baseline (Jun 610, Jul 590) roughly doubling to 1180 in August and 1260 in September, confirming the timing and magnitude of the surge that triggered this problem, but it is purely volume data and says nothing about the surge's underlying cause.

release_summary.summary: The requester (SH-CS, CL-01) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer dispute tickets and automatically fix wrong bills, framing the problem as a ticket-response-capacity issue. Investigation established instead that dispute tickets roughly doubled from a ~600/month baseline to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-05), that 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) carry an ACTUAL read type rather than a missing/estimated read (E-02), that tariff changes were ruled out (E-04) and ticket response times are within SLA (E-03), and that AMI read-event data (E-11) shows most of the ESTIMATED-read disputes also stem from a billing-import rejection rather than field read failures. This supports H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE: a change to billing import validation rules around August is the likely driver. Given this, the released solution is limited to the two parts of the plan that could be safely completed: cross-referencing dispute tickets against billing context and sending automated template responses (DA-TICKET), with no automated bill writes (K-BILLWRITE forbids this). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, issued under a DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS, because the CRITICAL VOB confirming exactly which billing rule changed (VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-IDENTITY) is still OPEN but its blocking scope (billing-rule diagnosis work) falls outside what is actually being released. A verification check also found that some of the limitation text itself is stale: it still describes AMI data work as blocked by degraded tool health and field-route work as blocked by an open VOB, when in fact the AMI tool is now healthy (and that query already ran, E-11) and the field-route VOB is now resolved.

output.summary: The requester (SH-CS, CL-01) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer dispute tickets and automatically fix wrong bills, framing the problem as a ticket-response-capacity issue. Investigation established instead that dispute tickets roughly doubled from a ~600/month baseline to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-05), that 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) carry an ACTUAL read type rather than a missing/estimated read (E-02), that tariff changes were ruled out (E-04) and ticket response times are within SLA (E-03), and that AMI read-event data (E-11) shows most of the ESTIMATED-read disputes also stem from a billing-import rejection rather than field read failures. This supports H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE: a change to billing import validation rules around August is the likely driver. Given this, the released solution is limited to the two parts of the plan that could be safely completed: cross-referencing dispute tickets against billing context and sending automated template responses (DA-TICKET), with no automated bill writes (K-BILLWRITE forbids this). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, issued under a DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS, because the CRITICAL VOB confirming exactly which billing rule changed (VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-IDENTITY) is still OPEN but its blocking scope (billing-rule diagnosis work) falls outside what is actually being released. A verification check also found that some of the limitation text itself is stale: it still describes AMI data work as blocked by degraded tool health and field-route work as blocked by an open VOB, when in fact the AMI tool is now healthy (and that query already ran, E-11) and the field-route VOB is now resolved.
key_points: Original request (CL-01, SH-CS): dispute tickets doubled since August; build an agent that auto-answers tickets and fixes wrong bills - this framing was treated as a hypothesis to test, not a fact.
Evidence confirms the surge: dispute volume went from a ~600/month baseline to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-05).
59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) have an ACTUAL read type, not a missing/estimated read, pointing to a billing-side defect rather than estimate substitution (E-02).
Alternative causes were checked and set aside: no tariff change occurred (E-04), and ticket response time is within SLA at 1.6-day median / 2.8-day p90 against a 3.0-day target (E-03).

AMI read-event data for the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes shows 1184 had a valid pre-cutoff read that billing import rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, reinforcing a billing-import rule defect rather than a field-read gap (E-11).

Released scope is limited to cross_reference_dispute_tickets and respond_to_dispute_tickets on DA-TICKET - automated ticket responses using already-cross-referenced billing context; no automated bill correction is included, consistent with K-BILLWRITE.

The decision RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION was made under a DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS, with the CRITICAL VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-IDENTITY (which billing rule changed) still OPEN but its blocking scope lying outside the released work items.
The field-route-to-dispute link VOB (VOB-U-FIELD-ROUTE-DISPUTE-LINK) has since been RESOLVED, unlike earlier text that still describes it as an open blocker.
limitations_explained: Which specific billing import rule changed, and whether its timing correlates with the August surge, is still unconfirmed - VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-IDENTITY remains OPEN and CRITICAL, so the exact defect has not been fixed or formally confirmed.

No automated bill correction/write is included: K-BILLWRITE requires any re-bill or credit to go through manual Billing Operations handling, so disputed bills themselves are not auto-corrected by this release.

A verification check flagged that some limitation statements are outdated: they say AMI/DA-MDMS work is excluded due to DEGRADED tool health, but mdms-export is now HEALTHY and that very query (E-11) already ran successfully.
Those same stale statements also say DA-ROUTE work is blocked by an OPEN VOB-U-FIELD-ROUTE-DISPUTE-LINK, but that VOB's status is now RESOLVED, so the stated blocker no longer applies as described.

Direct diagnosis of the billing-config rule-change log (DA-RULES) and detailed analysis of disputed ACTUAL-read bills (DA-BILL) were excluded from this release, originally due to an open critical VOB and unknown billing-config tool health.
Handoff validity for the field manual-read upload (H-FIELD-BILL) and the AMI nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) remains UNKNOWN and was not verified by this release.
Ticket response time is already within SLA (E-03), so the automated-response feature being released is not expected on its own to be the lever that brings dispute volume back to baseline.

Rolling back or correcting the billing rule itself (which would remove the root cause) is sequentially gated behind confirming the specific rule and was judged not completable within the remaining contest time.
